Resource Recovery
<u>General Motors Corporation (GM)</u>. GM included three publications that contained information leading to the recovery of materials from automobiles.
Analysis. No changes are needed to the EIS.

Fuel Economy Measurements
University of Michigan (UM). UM commented that the EPA test procedures do not seem to reflect real world fuel economy. A primary reason they cite is the lack of a variable road load setting for frontal area in the test procedure.
Analysis. Even if the test procedures are unrepresentative, they are prescribed by law. NHTSA has no authority to change the procedures. EPA test procedures for fuel economy do, in fact, include a variable factor for frontal area. This was included in EPA final rulemaking for MY 1979 light duty truck emissions.
Fuel Savings
National Conference of Governors'
Highway Safety Representatives. This Conference agreed with the fuel economy standard, which they concluded appeared reasonable. They also agreed that the standard will result in a substantial fuel savings.
